newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia PM to urge parliament to meet over reforms.
newsitem.headline: Russia PM to urge parliament to meet over reforms.

text.p: Russian Prime Minster Viktor Chernomyrdin said on Monday he will urge the State Duma lower house of parliament to break its summer vacations to consider the cabinet's reform package, Interfax news agency said.
The communist-dominated Duma went into a two-month summer recess last week after it had rejected several government bills aimed at boosting economic reform in Russia.

"I will try to discuss the need for an extraordinary session with the State Duma leadership tomorrow, and if necessary with the heads of parliamentary factions," Interfax quoted Chernomyrdin as saying.
Chernomyrdin told a news conference after the meeting of leadership of his centrist political party, Our Home is Russia, that he wants the Duma to meet soon after July 20.
Chernomyrdin said he wanted the deputies to discuss again the package of draft laws aimed at scrapping the Soveit-era welfare system which the chamber has rejected earlier.
The government argues that the huge welfare system, created as a safety net under for paternalistic Soviet system, has become too expensive for post-Communist Russia.

Chernomyrdin said that the adoption of the government's reform package was crucial for continuing the economic reform. He insisted that the cabinet could not wait until the end of parliamentary holidays.
